comments.text: Two inverse screen-code digits copied into the status display; Mystery Maze file variants share number25.
Initial placement-stream pointer consumed by resident $7514/$4D0F before the private initialization callback.
Background and border color bytes. Loader uses pristine backup $3804/$3805 when publishing VIC colors.
Seven-byte bomb record pointer. The scanner searches for key $FF; target count $3013 need not equal record count. PLF13 uniquely omits the terminator after its four intended records.
Four pending callback pointers copied by $758A into $40C8-$40CF. A zero high byte leaves the existing no-op task; nonzero vectors are committed by the resident IRQ.
Initial player X low, X high and Y in hardware sprite coordinates, read by spawn $56E0. This is the start of each life, not multicolor drawing coordinates.
Initial target counter 16. Collection decrements it; special bomb callbacks can compensate the decrement or replace the table. Primary record list has 16 entries.
Resident perimeter-bullet slot limit 0; $6800 considers sprite slots1 through limit-minus-one. Private level actors can use other slots.
Ordinary collection adds this little-endian binary value (100) to the24-bit total score. Private callbacks may add an extra award first.
Initial little-endian bonus 1500. The resident countdown subtracts100 per256 enabled IRQ services; completion adds the remaining amount to total and bonus records.
Private initialization routine called after initial scenery drawing. Common no-op target is the RTS at $301F.
Main-thread entry selected by JMP($301B) at $759C; typically the spawn/collection/exit loop at $3050.
Private cleanup hook copied into the local JSR trampoline before completion or exhaustion. A target of $301F returns immediately.
Shared one-byte RTS used by empty initialization, cleanup and individual bomb callbacks in this overlay.
Eight ladder/up-rope X columns followed by six down-rope X columns, copied to $40B0-$40BD. Coordinates use160-wide multicolor space; $FF marks unavailable columns.
Two zero header bytes between the climb-column arrays and completion vector; the shared loader does not read them as part of those arrays.
Ordinary successful-level destination $5B00. The private loop calls cleanup before jumping through this word.
Exhausted-lives destination $5FFD, the resident jump to game-over presentation $6A80. This is separate from successful completion.
Two filename suffix characters '13'. Resident loader copies them into $40D3/$40D4; private cleanup can replace them before the next disk request.
Single $FF drawing-stream terminator, used as the no-change post-bomb action.
Zero byte after the empty drawing terminator and before collection-key coordinate offsets.
X/Y offsets applied by resident $55BF when reducing player position to the bomb lookup key. They adjust the coarse cell test, not the visible bomb positions.
Optional hook called before the matched bomb-record callback. A zero high byte suppresses the call; otherwise the resident patches JSR $5643 from this word.
Twenty loaded zero bytes align the private main loop to $3050. Header fields end at $303B; no private structure is assigned to this gap.

Spawn Jumpman through$436A, repeatedly collect bombs through$436D, wait for the death controller to finish, respawn while reserve lives remain, otherwise call cleanup and use the elimination vector$3032. Zero remaining bombs freezes movement and uses completion vector$3030.
Load cleanup vector$301D/$301E into the operand of JSR$308B, invoke it, then return to the main-loop exit. Header targets the shared RTS$301F in this overlay.
On a player tick with life state0, any sprite collision involving the player requests death.

Drawing data $30A4-$3134 read by Initial scenery $30A4. Stream commands are FE shape pointer, FD repeat delta, FC stream jump, x/y/count placement and FF end. Referenced shapes hold width/x-offset/y-offset/pixel rows endingFF; source pixel codes are0 background,1 bomb,2 support,3 climbable. Parsed by the same behavioral renderer checked against original $4D0F.

16 seven-byte records [coarse key,x,y,callback low/high,post-draw low/high]. Terminator: $FF. Coordinates are160-wide bitmap positions. The resident scanner matches the key, calls both hooks, adds $3015 points, erases the bomb, follows the draw pointer and decrements $3013. This list is not bounded by the target counter.

Six packed30-byte multicolor creature frames. Pointer pairs$10/11,$12/13,$14/15 depict directional animation; expanded into sprite slots by initialization. Two further loader chunks contain unused state/route bytes.
Four entries each for Xlow delta,Xhigh delta,Y delta and base sprite pointer: up,right,down,left. The moving creature interpreter indexes these by command0..3.
Seven eight-byte arrays: duration,dx-low,dx-high,dy,base shape,route-pointer-low,route-pointer-high. Active indices4..7; initial pointers name$32B3,$32E9,$3319,$3349. Unused slots remain zero.
Four X-low positions, four X-high bytes, four Y positions and four colors for sprites4-7, indexed with biased bases in$33DA.
Incrementing IRQ counter; only values divisible by4 advance the four route-controlled creatures.

Interlinked three-byte motion programs. Commands0..3 choose direction and duration (third byte unused);$FF lo hi jumps unconditionally. Commands$10-$13 are conditional route branches: jump to their pointer and play sound when equal to player quadrant$3524, otherwise skip the triple. Initial four routes and all conditional destinations lie within this block.
Expand frames$31A6, then initialize sprites4-7 from position/color tables, choosing base pointer$10 and nonzero active flags.

Route update every fourth eligible callback through private $32B2 divider, independently of hazard pulse $402C; speed>=9 or life2 stops it. Ordinary/branch commands move immediately on selection; FF adds no stationary tick. CPU checked all96 triples and both outcomes of12 conditional commands over16384 callbacks.
Save current sprite index across a conditional-branch sound scheduling call.
On a matched quadrant branch, save X, request pulse stream$34EC at priority4, restore X and use command pointer bytes as the new route.
Envelope$22/$34, pulse$4444 followed by seven three-tick frequencies$2020,$E0E0,$4040,$C0C0,$6060,$A0A0,$8080, then0.
Set quadrant $3524 from hardwareX184 andY144 boundaries (half-X92). Below both gives$10; right adds1, below adds2; equality belongs to right/below. CPU checked every512x256 coordinate input.
Current player quadrant and creature animation counter. Route update increments the latter once per fourth-IRQ pass and uses bit0 for two-frame animation.

Retained file bytes, identical at these addresses to PLF10. Donor boundary comes from PLF08 $348C-$37FF (unused_level_eight_pattern_tail): Remaining loaded FF/00/80/7F buffer pattern, exactly matching PLF07. Not used by this level, whose only callback ends $30A3 and final redraw stream ends $323C. This copy has no established active control-flow or drawing target; it remains byte data. Packed-sprite overreads into unused slots are described at their active source blocks.
